extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A dataset containing 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reasoning about text to answer, aimed at facilitating progress on VQA models that can read text in images.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We set up a three stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing our data. In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text (using a forced-choice 'yes'/'no' flag). Filtering those (and noisy data from annotators) out resulted in 28,408 images, which form the basis of our TextVQA dataset. In the second stage, we collect 1-2 questions for each image. For the first question, we show annotators an image and ask them to provide a question which requires reading the text in the image to answer. To collect a second question that is different from the first, we show annotators the first question and ask them to come up with a question that requires reasoning about the text in the image and has a different answer. Following VQA and VizWiz datasets, we collect 10 answers for each question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: We use Open Images v3 dataset as the source of our images. We select categories that tend to have images with text in them (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard) by sampling images and running an OCR model to compute average number of OCR boxes per category, using these as weights for sampling.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To ensure answer quality, we gave annotators instructions similar to those used in VQA and VizWiz datasets when collecting the answers. In addition, to catch any poor quality data from earlier steps, we give annotators these four options: (i) no text in image; (ii) not a question; (iii) answering the question doesn't require reading any text in image; and (iv) unanswerable, e.g. questions involving speculation about the meaning of text. We remove the questions where a majority of workers marked any of these flags. Additionally, we use hand-crafted questions for which we know the correct answers to identify and filter out bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Following VQA and VizWiz datasets, we collect 10 answers for each question. Annotators were instructed to provide answers that require reading text in the image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on most common answer for 97.9% questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The focus of this paper is endowing Visual Question Answering (VQA) models a new capability – the ability to read text in images and answer questions by reasoning over the text and other visual content. This is important for applications involving aiding visually impaired users, as studies show up to 21% of questions asked by visually impaired users involve reading text in images.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset does not have significant biases w.r.t. images and questions, as indicated by low accuracies for question-only and image-only baselines.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Our OCR model, while mature, still fails at detecting text that is rotated, a bit unstructured (e.g., a scribble) or partially occluded. 8.9% of the TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens; we leave this as future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: To study the task of answering questions that require reading text in images, we collect a new dataset called TextVQA which is publicly available at https://textvqa.org. It is designed to benchmark progress on VQA models that can read and reason about text in images.
